clue.text: Small article by Dali in Central American capital

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
an is the indefinite article
the first name of the surrealist painter Salvador Dali

explanation.surface: A small piece of writing by the painter Dali turns up in a Central American city.
explanation.definitionFit: San Salvador is the capital city of El Salvador, a country in Central America.

clue.text: Health resort in a European country

blocks.note: a spa is a resort with healing waters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A health spa in a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a country in south-western Europe.

clue.text: Complex calculations made by anaesthetist? Crisis in middle of surgery

indicators.note: 'middle of' keeps only the middle letter of 'surgery'

blocks.note: playfully, one who numbs, a numb-er
a crunch is a crisis point
taken as written
the central letter of surgery

explanation.surface: An anaesthetist does complicated sums when a crisis strikes mid-operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: an anaesthetist numbs, so is read as a numb-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Number-crunching is the informal term for doing large amounts of complicated arithmetic.

clue.text: Group of characters in sacred river requiring help

blocks.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan
to abet is to help

explanation.surface: A band of people stuck in a holy river need assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Xanadu did Kubla Khan... where Alph, the sacred river, ran' is the source of this crossword standby.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is the full set of letters, a group of written characters.

clue.text: House housing a bad-tempered woman

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside

blocks.note: Virgo is one of the twelve astrological houses, the signs of the zodiac
taken as written

explanation.surface: A house is home to a shrewish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: House looks like a building, but here it is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, violent or bad-tempered woman.

clue.text: Craftily, trader tempts one in a place on the high street

definitions.text: a place on the high street

indicators.note: doing something craftily means by cunning manipulation, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A cunning shopkeeper lures a customer into a high-street shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The high street is the British name for a town's main shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: A department store is a large shop selling many kinds of goods, typical of a town's main shopping street.

clue.text: Shrub grew on church official

blocks.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to grow higher
an elder is an officer in some churches, such as Presbyterian ones

explanation.surface: A shrub grew up against a church officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose elder is the guelder rose, a flowering shrub of the viburnum family.

clue.text: Rodent, second seen in trade centre

indicators.note: something seen in a place appears inside it

blocks.note: a mart is a market, a trading centre
a mo is an informal word for a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A rodent is spotted briefly at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmot is a large burrowing rodent of the squirrel family.

clue.text: A free BBC?

blocks.note: taken as written
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: Asking whether the BBC is free to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC, so the question mark marks a definition by nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, is a long-standing affectionate nickname for the British Broadcasting Corporation.

clue.text: Put the wind up a member crossing line

indicators.note: one thing crossing another is laid across its middle, so the words before go round the word after

blocks.note: taken as written
an arm is a limb, a member of the body
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone frightens a club member who is crossing a picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: The line goes between the A and the limb word.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the wind up someone is an idiom for scaring them, which is what to alarm means.

clue.text: Father in capital wants us brought over together

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it
something brought over is turned upside down in a down-the-page sense, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the capital of France
pa is an informal word for father
taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: A father living in the capital wants the rest of us to come over and join him.
explanation.walkthrough: The father word sits between the I and the S of the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pari passu is a Latin phrase meaning side by side, at the same rate or on an equal footing.

clue.text: Chap was the leader, coming over and heading for Admiral Nelson

indicators.note: coming over suggests turning round, so the word for was the leader is read backwards
the heading of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a chap is a man
the leader led
the first letter of Admiral

explanation.surface: A man who led others is now heading for Admiral Nelson's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Nelson looks like one naval hero, but Admiral only supplies a letter and Nelson is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was the South African statesman, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: Gent has arm in an article of clothing

indicators.note: the gent has the limb in him, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentleman has his arm in his coat sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any single item of clothing, such as a coat or shirt.

clue.text: Stateswoman - chat nervously with her after start of tribunal

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
acting nervously means fidgeting and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of tribunal
the four letters of chat rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous person chats with a female politician once the tribunal begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The tribunal letter comes first, though the clue places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was the British prime minister from 1979 to 1990, a leading stateswoman.

clue.text: A ring brought in by governess for a religious leader

indicators.note: something brought in by another is taken inside it

blocks.note: an ayah is a nanny or governess in South Asia
an atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef

explanation.surface: A wedding ring delivered by the governess for a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A ring' looks like jewellery or the letter O, but it is a ring-shaped island.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shia Muslim cleric in Iran.

clue.text: Streak across mud, getting immersed

indicators.note: something immersed lies submerged within the surrounding words, so the letters sit buried inside the run of the clue

blocks.note: the letters run on from the end of the first word, through the second, into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone streaks naked across a muddy field and ends up plunging in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streak' suggests running naked, but it is the noun for a dirty mark; the comma after mud is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a blurred dirty mark or smear, the kind of streak a muddy finger leaves.

clue.text: Short signs for wrong and right beneath a puzzle

indicators.note: short means cut off, so each of the mark words loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written; it sits on top in a down answer
a cross marks a wrong answer
a tick marks a right answer

explanation.surface: A teacher's brief marks of wrong and right appear under a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, beneath means after, so the shortened marks follow the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which the first letters of lines spell out a word.

clue.text: American after a taxi back? You can count on it!

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the taxi word is read backwards
after places the American word behind the rest, so it is written last

blocks.note: taken as written
a cab is a taxi
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: An American hops into a taxi going back, and you can rely on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can count on it' reads as an assurance, but literally it describes a counting frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on wires used for doing arithmetic, so people literally count on it.

clue.text: Delegate, a southern character

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for southern
a sign is a written character or symbol

explanation.surface: A delegate is described as a southern sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: Delegate looks like a noun for a representative; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to assign it to someone else.

clue.text: So, a nicer new storyline

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters before are rearranged into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A writer is told the new version of the plot is a nicer one.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline plot of a film or play, a storyline.

clue.text: Key man, first to bat

blocks.note: first meaning: something that unlocks
second meaning: the cricketer who starts the batting innings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Key man' reads as one important person, but it splits into two meanings. In cricket, the batsmen who begin an innings are its openers.
explanation.definitionFit: A key or tin-opener is something that opens, and in cricket an opener bats first.

clue.text: Means to support a learner driver, whatever the circumstances

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the plate shown by a British learner driver
ways are means or methods

explanation.surface: Ways of helping a learner driver, no matter what happens.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a word that supports another sits below it, so the means word comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at all times, in every case regardless of the circumstances.

clue.text: Long-suffering patient, uncomplaining

blocks.note: first sense: bearing hardship for a long time
second sense: enduring calmly without protest

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a hospital patient, but every word is a near-synonym of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoics taught calm endurance of pain, so a stoical person bears trouble without complaint.

clue.text: Look at our Sunday paper, endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: the Everyman crossword is published in the Observer, the Sunday newspaper

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a look at this Sunday newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' is fair because this crossword appeared in the Observer, a British Sunday paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to watch or notice it, the same as looking at it.

clue.text: Hot drink, not busker's first

indicators.note: not means without, so the stated letter is removed
'first' keeps only the first letter of 'busker'

blocks.note: brandy is a spirit to drink
the opening letter of busker

explanation.surface: A busker turns down a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot drink' looks like one phrase, but hot is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for lustful or sexually aroused, a sense hot also carries.

clue.text: Irritation shown by terrible Russian chap having little time to gad about

blocks.note: gall is a sore or irritation
Ivan the Terrible was a Russian tsar
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A dreadful Russian man, short of time, is irritated enough to go off gadding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like a judgement on the Russian, but it pins down Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to wander about pleasure-seeking, which is what gadding about means.

clue.text: The snow leopard, at one time around for all to see

indicators.note: one word placed around another encloses it

blocks.note: once means formerly
U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: The snow leopard was once out in the open for everyone to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounce is an old alternative name for the snow leopard of Central Asia.

clue.text: Excellent company making film

blocks.note: high means superior, of excellent quality
a society is a company or association

explanation.surface: Fine company made it possible to shoot a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent company' also means the answer, but the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: High Society is the 1956 musical film starring Bing Crosby, Grace Kelly and Frank Sinatra.
